title: removeOne() with a negative index removes the wrong element and corrupts the queue
property: removeOne(i) behaves like Array.prototype.splice(i,1) on the equivalent array, including negative indices, leaving the remaining items intact
actual: returns 2 but the queue becomes [undefined, 1]-like corrupted state (the front slot is cleared and head advanced instead of removing the last item)
evidence: removeOne explicitly accepts negative indices (range check i < -size, then i += size), and peekAt documents negative indices as counting from the end. The shifting branch is chosen with the un-normalised `index` (index < size/2), so a negative index always takes the front branch with a zero-iteration loop.

title: remove() with a negative index and count > 1 removes the wrong items and corrupts the queue
property: remove(i, n) behaves like Array.prototype.splice(i, n), including negative i
actual: queue is left with undefined holes and wrong contents
evidence: remove() accepts negative indices (i < -size check, i += size) but the later branches use the raw `index` (index + count === size, index === 0, index < 0) instead of the normalised i.
